response.text:
I can do that — but I need a few things before I can publish (and I can’t act in the background or publish without explicit access/confirmation).

Please choose one of these two options and supply the requested details:

Option A — I publish it for you
- Confirm you want this posted publicly now to your status page.
- Target status page: URL + provider (e.g., statuspage.io, Atlassian Statuspage, custom site).  
- Access: tell me how I should authenticate (or confirm you’ll grant the connector/tool access). Do NOT paste secrets or tokens into chat unless your system explicitly supports secure connector sharing — if you intend to provide credentials here, I’ll instead ask you to use the secure integration UI.
- Exact content to publish: paste the approved incident writeup here or provide a link to the approved document. (If there are any redactions required, list them.)
- Title/headline to use (or say “use the document title”).
- Visibility/tags: public vs. internal, component(s) to mark affected, severity tag, and whether to add “postmortem” label.
- Publish timing: publish immediately or schedule (date/time, timezone).
- Any links to include (full internal report, follow-up actions, mitigations).
- Confirm you have authority to publish this publicly and that no sensitive data (customer PII, internal credentials) is included.

Option B — I prepare the public post for you to paste/publish
- Paste or link the approved incident writeup (or tell me to draft a concise public version from the approved writeup).
- Tell me preferred title, length (short status update vs. full postmortem), and any points to emphasize/omit (e.g., customer-impact numbers, mitigations).
I’ll return a ready-to-publish status-page post in the format most status pages accept (short summary + timeline + follow-ups + links) you can paste into the status page UI.

What would you like to do? If Option A, provide the access method and content; if Option B, paste the approved writeup (or say “use the approved writeup” if it’s already attached).
